findings.reason: the property should be renamed (or the existing routed-IDS field extended) so one vocabulary covers both, otherwise §8's prompt and §9's counts read an ambiguous field.
findings.text: §11 adds an edge property `arm` (values `retrieval`|`cluster`), but the MAPPING_CANDIDATE edge already carries "the routed IDS and its Choice probability" (facility.yaml:1913-1916) and imas_codex/ids/candidates.py:78 already defines `Candidate.arms` as the set of routed/IDS arms that returned a hit; the same word now names two different axes on the same edge and module, so a reader of the prompt (§8) or the §9 home-source count cannot tell which "arm" a value means — the owner to extend is the existing routed-IDS property on the edge and `Candidate.arms`, not a parallel property

findings.reason: §11 must state in its own text what the added property/refusal retires or merges, or why nothing can be, to match §8's accounting.
findings.text: with the week's supplied figures at public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0, §11 adds surface (the `arm` schema property, and a write_candidates refusal when `arm` is neither `retrieval` nor `cluster`, §11 done-when) while naming only that "No setting is added" and specifying no retirement or merge — §8 by contrast accounts for its surface by retiring --skip-metadata/--skip-errors, mapping_target_path/ids/type, create_signal_source and count_sources_by_mapping_status

findings.reason: the concepts do not overlap, so naming node_classifier would be a citation nicety rather than a reuse the plan should adopt.
findings.text: §8 derives TargetType in a new classmethod on TargetType (imas_codex/ids/models.py:44) fed by section fields without citing imas_codex/core/node_classifier.py, whose docstring claims to be the "single source of truth" for DD node classification; the search shows the two are different axes (node_classifier emits node_category: quantity/geometry/identifier/coordinate, while TargetType is struct_array/time_slice/scalar/profile), so the owner cannot in fact be extended and no code change is owed

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the candidate stage stays behind imas_codex/ids/candidates.py (retrieve_candidates, route_ids, judge_candidates, route over three small frozen dataclasses), and §11 places its cluster expansion in that same module beside retrieve_candidates rather than in a new one, so behaviour is hidden behind a handful of functions rather than spread over parallel wrappers.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §11 adds a second meaning of "arm" on the same edge and module that already carry a routed-IDS/arms vocabulary.
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; §11 adds a facility.yaml schema property (`arm`) and a new write_candidates refusal without naming what it retires or merges, or why nothing can be.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — §4 reuses hybrid_dd_search through retrieve_candidates (imas_codex/ids/candidates.py:120), §11 reuses related_dd_search(..., relationship_types="cluster") (imas_codex/graph/dd_search.py:606) rather than writing a second cluster query, and §8 reuses claim_batch (imas_codex/discovery/base/claims.py:255), write_mapping_binding/clear_mapping_bindings (imas_codex/ids/graph_ops.py:552,621) and fetch_cross_facility_mappings (imas_codex/ids/tools.py:733); the plan cites each by name, and the only uncited neighbour is node_classifier.py, which classifies a different axis.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — read_candidates and select_candidates (§8, map-context-reads-candidates) are not wrappers over an existing reader; a grep for MAPPING_CANDIDATE shows no reader exists today (only write_candidates/count/clear in graph_ops.py), and the plan states why select_candidates cannot be write_candidates (write_candidates deletes and rewrites every edge, a pick must flag existing edges without disturbing the shortlist).
